subject: cs1
title: Aim of Descriptive Analysis
prompt: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of descriptive data analysis?
options: To summarize and present key features of a dataset
solution: Descriptive analysis focuses on summarising and describing the main characteristics of a dataset using statistics and visualisations.

subject: cs1
title: Inferential Data Analysis
prompt: Which of the following activities is most closely associated with inferential data analysis?
options: Sorting raw data into ascending order
Estimating population parameters from sample data
solution: Inferential analysis draws conclusions about a population based on a sample, such as estimating parameters or testing hypotheses.

subject: cs1
title: Predictive Data Analysis
prompt: Which of the following is an example of predictive data analysis?
options: Using past sales data to forecast future revenue
Calculating the mean of historical profits
solution: Predictive analysis uses historical data to make predictions about future outcomes.

subject: cs1
title: Exploratory Data Analysis Stage
prompt: Which stage of data analysis primarily focuses on detecting patterns, anomalies and relationships?
solution: Exploratory data analysis (EDA) involves visualisations and summary statistics to explore structure and relationships in the data.

subject: cs1
title: Visualising a Single Continuous Variable
prompt: Which of the following tools is most appropriate for visualising the distribution of a single continuous variable?
solution: A histogram displays the frequency distribution of a continuous variable.

subject: cs1
title: Robust Measure of Location
prompt: Which of the following is a robust measure of central tendency?
solution: The median is robust because it is not sensitive to extreme values or outliers.

subject: cs1
title: Measuring Spread About the Mean
prompt: Which statistic measures the spread of data around its mean?
solution: Variance measures the average squared deviation from the mean.

subject: cs1
title: Measuring Linear Association
prompt: Which of the following correlation measures assesses linear association between two variables?
solution: Pearson’s correlation measures the strength of linear association between two continuous variables.

subject: cs1
title: Rank-Based Correlation
prompt: Which correlation measure is based on ranked data?
solution: Spearman’s correlation uses the ranks of the data rather than the raw values.

subject: cs1
title: Purpose of Principal Component Analysis
prompt: Which of the following best describes the purpose of principal component analysis (PCA)?
options: To reduce dimensionality while retaining most variability
solution: PCA transforms correlated variables into a smaller number of uncorrelated components capturing most of the variance.

subject: cs1
title: Meaning of Reproducible Research
prompt: Which of the following best describes the meaning of reproducible research?
options: Ensuring that the same results can be obtained using the same data and analysis steps
Using multiple datasets to confirm conclusions
solution: Reproducible research ensures that independent analysts can obtain the same results when given the same data and methods.

subject: cs1
title: Essentials of Reproducible Analysis
prompt: Which of the following is an essential element of reproducible data analysis?
options: Documenting code, data sources and analysis procedures
solution: Clear documentation of data, code and methodology is fundamental to reproducibility.

subject: cs1
title: Defining Extremely Large Data Sets
prompt: Which of the following best describes extremely large data sets?
options: Any dataset with more than 1,000 observations
Datasets whose size or complexity exceeds the capabilities of traditional data-processing tools
Only datasets stored in cloud systems
solution: Extremely large datasets require specialised storage, processing and analytical techniques.

subject: cs1
title: Summarising Skewed Income Data
prompt: Which summary statistic is most appropriate for describing skewed income data?
solution: The median is resistant to extreme values and better represents central tendency for skewed distributions.

subject: cs1
title: Spotting Outliers Graphically
prompt: Which plot is most useful for identifying potential outliers?
solution: Boxplots display quartiles and highlight potential outliers using fences.

subject: cs1
title: Measuring Monotonic Association
prompt: Which statistic measures monotonic association between two variables?
solution: Spearman’s correlation captures monotonic relationships even when the relationship is not linear.

subject: cs1
title: Kendall's Tau
prompt: Which statement about Kendall’s tau is correct?
options: It is identical to Pearson's correlation
It measures ordinal association based on concordant and discordant pairs
solution: Kendall’s tau quantifies ordinal association using the proportion of concordant and discordant pairs.

subject: cs1
title: First Principal Component
prompt: Which of the following is true about the first principal component in PCA?
options: It explains the maximum possible variance in the data
It is always aligned with the original axes
solution: The first principal component is the linear combination of variables capturing the greatest variance.

subject: cs1
title: Bivariate Data Visualisation
prompt: Which of the following is an appropriate tool for bivariate data visualisation?
solution: Scatter plots visualise relationships between two quantitative variables.

subject: cs1
title: Benefits of Data Visualisation
prompt: Which of the following is a key benefit of data visualisation?
options: It reveals patterns and relationships not obvious from raw numbers
It eliminates the need for models
solution: Visualisation aids understanding by revealing structure, trends and anomalies.

subject: cs1
title: Role of Data Cleaning
prompt: Which of the following best describes the role of data cleaning?
options: Identifying and correcting errors, missing values and inconsistencies
solution: Data cleaning improves data quality and reliability of subsequent analysis.

subject: cs1
title: Function of Summary Statistics
prompt: Which of the following best describes the function of summary statistics?
options: To condense large datasets into key numerical descriptors
solution: Summary statistics provide concise numerical information about location, spread and shape of data.

subject: cs1
title: Interquartile Range
prompt: Which of the following best describes the interquartile range (IQR)?
options: The difference between maximum and minimum values
The difference between the third and first quartiles
The average of squared deviations from the mean
solution: The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

subject: cs1
title: Correlation Pitfalls
prompt: Which of the following is true about correlation?
solution: Correlation measures association, not causality, and lies between -1 and 1.

subject: cs1
title: Purpose of the Data Analysis Process
prompt: Which of the following best summarises the purpose of the entire data analysis process?
options: To extract meaningful insights and support decision-making from data
solution: Data analysis transforms raw data into actionable insights for informed decisions.

subject: cs1
title: Geometric Memoryless Property
prompt: Which of the following is a property of a geometric distribution with success probability p?
options: Its mean is equal to its variance
solution: The geometric distribution is memoryless: $$P(X > m+n \mid X > m) = P(X > n).$$ It is the only discrete distribution with this property.

subject: cs1
title: Binomial Random Variable Definition
prompt: Which of the following best describes a binomial random variable?
options: Number of successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials
Number of failures before the r-th success
Number of events occurring in continuous time
solution: A binomial random variable counts the number of successes in n independent trials with success probability p.

subject: cs1
title: Binomial Variance
prompt: Which of the following is the variance of a $\text{Binomial}(n, p)$ distribution?
solution: For $X \sim \text{Bin}(n, p)$, $X$ is a sum of $n$ independent Bernoulli($p$) variables, each with variance $p(1-p)$, so $$E[X] = np, \qquad \text{Var}(X) = np(1-p).$$

subject: cs1
title: Counting Failures Before the r-th Success
prompt: Which distribution models the number of failures before the r-th success?
solution: The negative binomial distribution counts the number of failures before achieving a fixed number of successes.

subject: cs1
title: Hypergeometric vs Binomial
prompt: Which of the following distinguishes the hypergeometric distribution from the binomial distribution?
solution: The hypergeometric distribution models sampling without replacement from a finite population.

subject: cs1
title: Poisson Mean–Variance Property
prompt: Which of the following is a property of the Poisson distribution with parameter λ?
options: It is symmetric for all λ
solution: For X ~ Poisson(λ), E[X] = Var(X) = λ.

subject: cs1
title: Memoryless Continuous Distribution
prompt: Which continuous distribution is memoryless?
solution: The exponential distribution satisfies the memoryless property: P(X > s+t | X > s) = P(X > t).

subject: cs1
title: Sum of Independent Exponentials
prompt: Which distribution is the sum of k independent exponential random variables with common rate?
solution: If $X_1, \dots, X_k$ are independent $\text{Exp}(\lambda)$, then (e.g. by multiplying MGFs) $$\sum_{i=1}^k X_i \sim \text{Gamma}(k, \lambda).$$ The chi-square is only the special case $\lambda = \tfrac12$, so gamma is the general answer.

subject: cs1
title: Symmetry of the Normal Distribution
prompt: Which of the following is a property of the normal distribution?
options: It is skewed for all parameter values
It is symmetric about its mean
solution: The normal distribution is symmetric about its mean μ.

subject: cs1
title: Distribution on the Unit Interval
prompt: Which distribution has support on the interval (0, 1)?
solution: The beta distribution is defined on the interval (0,1).

subject: cs1
title: Waiting Time to the k-th Poisson Event
prompt: Which distribution describes the waiting time until the k-th event in a Poisson process?
solution: The waiting time to the k-th arrival in a Poisson process follows a gamma distribution.

subject: cs1
title: Poisson Process Assumptions
prompt: Which of the following best describes a Poisson process?
options: Events occur independently at a constant average rate
solution: A Poisson process assumes independent events occurring at a constant rate λ over time.

subject: cs1
title: Inverse Transform Simulation
prompt: Which method can be used to generate random variables from a given distribution using uniform random numbers?
solution: The inverse transform method uses the inverse CDF to generate samples from a distribution.

subject: cs1
title: Condition for Independence
prompt: Which condition is required for two random variables X and Y to be independent?
options: The joint distribution equals the product of the marginals
solution: $X$ and $Y$ are independent if and only if $$f_{X,Y}(x,y) = f_X(x)\,f_Y(y) \quad \text{for all } x, y.$$ Independence implies zero covariance and correlation, but zero covariance does not imply independence.

subject: cs1
title: Definition of Covariance
prompt: Which of the following correctly defines covariance?
solution: Covariance measures joint variability about the means: $$\text{Cov}(X,Y) = E\big[(X-E[X])(Y-E[Y])\big] = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y].$$

subject: cs1
title: Variance of a Linear Combination
prompt: Which of the following gives the variance of a linear combination $aX + bY$?
solution: $$\text{Var}(aX+bY) = a^2\,\text{Var}(X) + b^2\,\text{Var}(Y) + 2ab\,\text{Cov}(X,Y).$$ The covariance term vanishes only when $X$ and $Y$ are uncorrelated.

subject: cs1
title: Conditional Expectation
prompt: Which of the following best defines conditional expectation E[X | Y]?
options: The joint expectation of X and Y
The variance of X given Y
The expected value of X given a specific value of Y
solution: Conditional expectation incorporates information about Y when computing the expected value of X.

subject: cs1
title: Law of Total Expectation
prompt: Which of the following identities is known as the law of total expectation?
solution: The law of total expectation (tower property) states $$E[X] = E\big[E[X \mid Y]\big],$$ i.e. the mean of $X$ is the average of its conditional means.

subject: cs1
title: Uniqueness of the MGF
prompt: Which function uniquely determines the distribution of a random variable (when it exists)?
solution: The moment generating function, when it exists in a neighbourhood of zero, uniquely determines the distribution.

subject: cs1
title: Normal Limit of Sums
prompt: Which theorem explains why the sum of many independent random variables tends toward a normal distribution?
solution: The Central Limit Theorem describes convergence in distribution to the normal distribution.

subject: cs1
title: What Is a Sampling Distribution?
prompt: Which of the following best describes a sampling distribution?
options: The joint distribution of all variables
The distribution of a statistic over repeated samples
The distribution of the raw data
solution: A sampling distribution describes how a statistic varies across repeated samples.

subject: cs1
title: Sample Mean from a Normal Population
prompt: Which is the distribution of the sample mean from a normal population with known variance?
solution: The sample mean from a normal population is normally distributed.

subject: cs1
title: Distribution of the Sample Variance
prompt: Which distribution does the sample variance (scaled appropriately) follow for normal data?
solution: For a random sample of size $n$ from $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$: $$\frac{(n-1)S^2}{\sigma^2} \sim \chi^2_{n-1}.$$

subject: cs1
title: Ratio of Two Sample Variances
prompt: Which distribution describes the ratio of two independent sample variances from normal populations, each divided by its population variance?
solution: $$\frac{S_1^2/\sigma_1^2}{S_2^2/\sigma_2^2} \sim F_{n_1-1,\; n_2-1},$$ since it is a ratio of independent chi-square variables, each divided by its degrees of freedom.

subject: cs1
title: Studentised Sample Mean
prompt: Which statistic follows a t distribution for a normal population with unknown variance?
options: The standardized sample mean using the sample variance
solution: When $\sigma$ is unknown it is replaced by $S$, and $$\frac{\bar X - \mu}{S/\sqrt{n}} \sim t_{n-1}.$$

subject: cs1
title: Method of Moments
prompt: Which of the following best describes the method of moments?
options: Equating sample moments to population moments to estimate parameters
Matching quantiles of the sample and population
solution: The method of moments constructs estimators by setting sample moments equal to theoretical moments.

subject: cs1
title: Defining the MLE
prompt: Which of the following defines the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE)?
options: The parameter value that minimises bias
The parameter value that maximises the sample mean
The parameter value that maximises the likelihood function
The parameter value that minimises the variance
solution: MLE chooses the parameter value that makes the observed data most probable.

subject: cs1
title: Unbiased Estimators
prompt: Which property of an estimator means that its expected value equals the true parameter?
solution: An estimator $\hat\theta$ is unbiased if $E[\hat\theta] = \theta$, i.e. its bias $E[\hat\theta] - \theta$ is zero.

subject: cs1
title: Consistency of an Estimator
prompt: Which of the following best describes consistency of an estimator?
options: The estimator is unbiased for all sample sizes
The estimator has zero mean square error
The estimator converges in probability to the true parameter as sample size increases
solution: Consistency means $\hat\theta \to \theta$ in probability as $n \to \infty$. A sufficient condition is that $\text{MSE}(\hat\theta) \to 0$.

subject: cs1
title: Bias–Variance Decomposition of MSE
prompt: Which of the following correctly defines the mean squared error of an estimator?
solution: $$\text{MSE}(\hat\theta) = E\big[(\hat\theta - \theta)^2\big] = \text{Var}(\hat\theta) + \big[\text{bias}(\hat\theta)\big]^2.$$ Note $E[\hat\theta - \theta]$ is the bias itself, not the MSE.

subject: cs1
title: Efficient Estimators
prompt: Which statement about an efficient estimator is correct?
options: It has minimum MSE among all estimators, biased or unbiased
It has the smallest variance among all unbiased estimators
It is always the method of moments estimator
solution: Efficiency compares variances within the class of unbiased estimators: an efficient (minimum variance unbiased) estimator has the smallest variance in that class, e.g. it attains the Cramér–Rao lower bound. A biased estimator may still have a smaller MSE.

subject: cs1
title: Asymptotic Properties of MLEs
prompt: Which of the following is an asymptotic property of MLEs?
solution: Under regularity conditions, MLEs are asymptotically normal.

subject: cs1
title: The Bootstrap
prompt: Which of the following best describes the bootstrap method?
options: Resampling with replacement from the observed data to estimate properties of an estimator
Generating random numbers from known distributions
Using asymptotic theory to approximate distributions
solution: The bootstrap approximates the sampling distribution via resampling the observed data.

subject: cs1
title: Interpreting a 95% Confidence Interval
prompt: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of a 95% confidence interval?
options: The probability the true parameter lies in this specific interval is 95%
95% of the data lie inside the interval
95% of such intervals constructed from repeated samples will contain the true parameter
The true parameter equals the midpoint with 95% probability
solution: The confidence level refers to long-run frequency of correct intervals.

subject: cs1
title: Interval for a Future Observation
prompt: Which interval is used to estimate the range of a future observation?
solution: Prediction intervals account for both parameter uncertainty and observation variability.

subject: cs1
title: CI for a Normal Mean, Variance Unknown
prompt: Which distribution is used for a confidence interval for the mean of a normal population with unknown variance?
solution: The t distribution is used when σ is unknown.

subject: cs1
title: Comparing Two Normal Variances
prompt: Which test is appropriate for comparing two population variances from normal samples?
solution: The ratio of sample variances follows an F distribution under normality.

subject: cs1
title: Type I Error
prompt: Which of the following defines a Type I error?
options: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis
solution: Type I error occurs when a true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected.

subject: cs1
title: Probability of a Type I Error
prompt: Which quantity represents the probability of a Type I error?
solution: The significance level α is the probability of rejecting H₀ when it is true.

subject: cs1
title: Power of a Test
prompt: Which of the following defines the power of a test?
options: The probability that the null hypothesis is true
The probability of rejecting a false null hypothesis
The probability of a Type II error
The probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis
solution: Power equals 1 − β, where β is the probability of a Type II error.

subject: cs1
title: Interpreting the p-Value
prompt: Which of the following best describes the p-value?
options: The probability that H₀ is true
The probability of observing a test statistic as extreme or more extreme under H₀
The probability of a Type I error
The probability that H₁ is true
solution: The p-value measures the strength of evidence against the null hypothesis.

subject: cs1
title: Goodness-of-Fit Testing
prompt: Which test is used to assess whether a sample follows a specified distribution?
solution: The chi-square goodness-of-fit test compares observed and expected frequencies.

subject: cs1
title: Testing Independence in a Contingency Table
prompt: Which test is used to assess independence in a contingency table?
solution: The chi-square test of independence is applied to contingency tables.

subject: cs1
title: Permutation Tests
prompt: Which non-parametric testing approach is based on rearranging the observed data?
solution: Permutation tests construct the null distribution by rearranging the observed data.

subject: cs1
title: Simple Null Hypothesis
prompt: Which of the following best describes a simple null hypothesis?
options: A hypothesis that completely specifies the distribution
A hypothesis that leaves some parameters unspecified
A hypothesis that can never be tested
solution: A simple hypothesis fully specifies the probability model.

subject: cs1
title: Composite Hypotheses
prompt: Which statement about composite hypotheses is correct?
options: They leave at least one parameter unspecified
solution: Composite hypotheses do not fully specify the distribution.

subject: cs1
title: Sensitivity of a Diagnostic Test
prompt: Which concept measures the ability of a diagnostic test to correctly identify positives?
solution: Sensitivity measures the true positive rate.

subject: cs1
title: Specificity of a Diagnostic Test
prompt: Which concept measures the ability of a diagnostic test to correctly identify negatives?
solution: Specificity measures the true negative rate.

subject: cs1
title: Likelihood Ratio Test Statistic
prompt: Which of the following correctly defines the likelihood ratio test statistic, where $L_0$ and $L_1$ are the maximised likelihoods under $H_0$ and $H_1$?
solution: $$-2\log\frac{L_0}{L_1} = 2(\ell_1 - \ell_0),$$ where $\ell = \log L$. For nested models it is approximately $\chi^2$ with degrees of freedom equal to the difference in the number of parameters.

subject: cs1
title: Critical Region
prompt: Which of the following best describes a critical region?
options: The region containing the true parameter
The region where p-values are computed
The set of values of the test statistic for which H₀ is rejected
solution: The critical region determines the decision rule of the test.

subject: cs1
title: Response Variable
prompt: Which of the following best defines the response variable in a regression model?
options: The variable used to explain another variable
The variable being explained or predicted
The variable that has no randomness
The variable that is fixed by design
solution: The response variable (dependent variable) is the outcome the model aims to explain or predict.

subject: cs1
title: Explanatory Variable
prompt: Which of the following best defines the explanatory variable in regression?
options: The variable used to explain variation in the response
solution: Explanatory variables (independent variables) explain variation in the response variable.

subject: cs1
title: Simple Linear Regression Model
prompt: Which of the following correctly states the simple linear regression model?
solution: The simple linear regression model is $Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i + \varepsilon_i$, relating the response $Y$ to the explanatory variable $x$ with intercept $\beta_0$, slope $\beta_1$ and random error $\varepsilon$.

subject: cs1
title: Ordinary Least Squares Criterion
prompt: Which method is used to estimate the regression coefficients in ordinary least squares?
options: Minimising the sum of squared residuals
solution: Ordinary least squares chooses coefficients that minimise the sum of squared residuals.

subject: cs1
title: Least Squares Slope Estimator
prompt: Which of the following is the least squares estimator of the slope $\beta_1$ in simple linear regression?
solution: Minimising $\sum (y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 x_i)^2$ gives $$\hat\beta_1 = \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}} = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar x)(y_i - \bar y)}{\sum (x_i - \bar x)^2}, \qquad \hat\beta_0 = \bar y - \hat\beta_1 \bar x.$$ $\sum x_i y_i / \sum x_i^2$ is the estimator for a line forced through the origin.

subject: cs1
title: Classical Regression Assumptions
prompt: Which of the following is a key assumption of the classical linear regression model?
options: The errors have mean zero and constant variance
The regression line always passes through the origin
The response variable is normally distributed
solution: Homoscedasticity and zero-mean errors are core regression assumptions.

subject: cs1
title: Coefficient of Determination
prompt: Which of the following measures the proportion of variation in Y explained by the regression model?
solution: $R^2 = SS_{\text{REG}}/SS_{\text{TOT}}$ is the proportion of the total variation in $Y$ explained by the regression.

subject: cs1
title: Significance of a Regression Coefficient
prompt: Which test is usually used to assess whether an individual regression coefficient, such as the slope, is statistically significant?
solution: Under $H_0: \beta_1 = 0$, $$t = \frac{\hat\beta_1}{\text{s.e.}(\hat\beta_1)} \sim t_{n-2}$$ in simple linear regression. (The ANOVA F-test is equivalent there, with $F = t^2$.)

subject: cs1
title: Residuals vs Fitted Values Plot
prompt: Which plot is most useful for checking linearity and homoscedasticity?
options: Scatter plot of X and Y
solution: Residual plots reveal violations of regression assumptions.

subject: cs1
title: Multicollinearity
prompt: Which of the following best describes multicollinearity?
options: Nonlinear relationship between X and Y
solution: Multicollinearity occurs when predictors are highly correlated.

subject: cs1
title: Categorical Explanatory Variable
prompt: Which of the following is an example of a categorical explanatory variable?
solution: Categorical variables take distinct categories rather than numerical values.

subject: cs1
title: Exponential Family Models in GLMs
prompt: Which of the following regression models is a GLM whose response distribution is a non-normal member of the exponential family?
solution: Poisson regression uses a Poisson response (an exponential-family distribution) with a log link. The normal linear model is also a GLM, which made the original wording ambiguous; ridge and lasso are penalised least squares methods with normal errors.

subject: cs1
title: Canonical Link for the Poisson
prompt: Which of the following is the canonical link function for the Poisson distribution?
solution: The canonical link for Poisson models is the log link.

subject: cs1
title: Fitting Criterion for GLMs
prompt: Which quantity is minimised when fitting a GLM?
solution: GLMs are fitted by maximum likelihood, which is equivalent to minimising the deviance (twice the gap in log-likelihood between the saturated model and the fitted model). For the normal model this reduces to least squares.

subject: cs1
title: Deviance Residuals
prompt: Which residual is used to assess overall model adequacy in GLMs?
solution: Deviance residuals assess goodness-of-fit in GLMs.

subject: cs1
title: Comparing Nested GLMs
prompt: Which test compares nested GLMs?
solution: For nested models, the difference in scaled deviances is approximately $\chi^2$ with degrees of freedom equal to the difference in the number of parameters. This is the likelihood ratio test. (An F-test is used instead when the scale parameter has to be estimated.)

subject: cs1
title: GLM Linear Predictor
prompt: Which of the following defines the linear predictor $\eta$ in a GLM?
solution: The linear predictor is $\eta = \mathbf{x}^{\top}\boldsymbol\beta = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \dots + \beta_p x_p$. It is related to the mean by the link function, $g(\mu) = \eta$.

subject: cs1
title: Detecting Non-Linearity
prompt: Which plot is useful for detecting non-linearity in regression?
solution: Patterns in residual plots indicate model inadequacy.

subject: cs1
title: Model Selection with Adjusted R-Squared
prompt: Which of the following is used for model selection in multiple regression?
solution: Adjusted $R^2$ penalises extra parameters, so unlike $R^2$ it does not automatically increase when a predictor is added.

subject: cs1
title: Interaction Terms
prompt: Which of the following statements about interaction terms is correct?
options: They allow the effect of one variable to depend on another
solution: Interaction terms capture dependence between predictors.

subject: cs1
title: Pearson Residuals
prompt: Which of the following best describes Pearson residuals?
options: Difference between predicted and mean response
Difference between fitted and true values
Difference between observed and predicted values
Standardised difference between observed and fitted values
solution: The Pearson residual is $$\frac{y - \hat\mu}{\sqrt{V(\hat\mu)}},$$ the raw residual divided by the estimated standard deviation under the model.

subject: cs1
title: GLM for Count Data
prompt: Which model is appropriate for count data in GLMs?
solution: Poisson regression is designed for modelling counts.

subject: cs1
title: Response Distribution in Logistic Regression
prompt: Which distribution is used in logistic regression?
solution: Logistic regression models binomial outcomes.

subject: cs1
title: Link Function in Logistic Regression
prompt: Which link function is used in logistic regression?
solution: The logit link relates probabilities to the linear predictor.

subject: cs1
title: Overdispersion in a Poisson GLM
prompt: Which of the following best describes overdispersion in a Poisson GLM?
options: The observed variance exceeds the model variance
The model has too many predictors
solution: Overdispersion occurs when data variability is larger than the Poisson assumption allows.

subject: cs1
title: What Is Bayesian Inference?
prompt: Which of the following best describes Bayesian inference?
options: Estimating parameters using only sample means
solution: Bayesian inference updates prior beliefs in light of observed data.

subject: cs1
title: Ingredients of Bayes' Theorem
prompt: Which components make up Bayes' theorem?
solution: Bayes’ theorem combines prior beliefs with data through the likelihood to obtain the posterior.

subject: cs1
title: Prior Distribution
prompt: Which distribution represents knowledge about a parameter before observing data?
solution: The prior reflects beliefs about the parameter before seeing data.

subject: cs1
title: Posterior Distribution
prompt: Which distribution represents updated beliefs after observing data?
solution: The posterior combines the prior and the likelihood.

subject: cs1
title: Normalising Constant in Bayes' Theorem
prompt: Which term in Bayes' theorem ensures the posterior integrates to one?
solution: The marginal likelihood acts as the normalising constant.

subject: cs1
title: Non-Informative Priors
prompt: Which type of prior is chosen to have minimal influence on the posterior, reflecting little or no prior knowledge?
solution: Non-informative priors aim to have minimal influence on the posterior.

subject: cs1
title: Conjugate Priors
prompt: Which prior leads to a posterior of the same functional form?
solution: Conjugate priors simplify Bayesian updating.

subject: cs1
title: Conjugate Prior for Binomial Data
prompt: Which distribution is conjugate to the binomial likelihood?
solution: The Beta distribution is conjugate to the Binomial.

subject: cs1
title: Conjugate Prior for Poisson Data
prompt: Which distribution is conjugate to the Poisson likelihood?
solution: The Gamma distribution is conjugate to the Poisson likelihood.

subject: cs1
title: Bayes Estimator Under Squared Error Loss
prompt: Which Bayesian estimator minimises expected squared error loss?
solution: The posterior mean minimises quadratic loss.

subject: cs1
title: Bayes Estimator Under Absolute Error Loss
prompt: Which Bayesian estimator minimises absolute error loss?
solution: The posterior median minimises absolute loss.

subject: cs1
title: Bayes Estimator Under All-or-Nothing Loss
prompt: Which Bayesian estimator minimises 0–1 loss?
solution: The MAP estimate minimises 0–1 loss.

subject: cs1
title: Posterior Predictive Distribution
prompt: Which distribution describes future observations given current data?
solution: The posterior predictive combines uncertainty in parameters and new data.

subject: cs1
title: Summarising the Posterior
prompt: Which quantity summarises the central tendency of the posterior distribution?
solution: The posterior mean is a key summary statistic.

subject: cs1
title: Credible Intervals
prompt: Which interval contains a fixed proportion of posterior probability?
solution: Credible intervals are Bayesian probability statements.

subject: cs1
title: Approximating Complex Posteriors
prompt: Which algorithm is commonly used for approximating complex posteriors?
solution: MCMC methods sample from complex posterior distributions.

subject: cs1
title: Metropolis–Hastings Algorithm
prompt: Which MCMC method uses proposal distributions and acceptance probabilities?
solution: Metropolis-Hastings generates samples using acceptance-rejection.

subject: cs1
title: Gibbs Sampler
prompt: Which MCMC method samples directly from conditional distributions?
solution: Gibbs sampling draws from full conditional distributions.

subject: cs1
title: Role of the Likelihood in Bayes' Theorem
prompt: In Bayes' theorem, $f(\theta \mid x) \propto f(x \mid \theta)\, f(\theta)$. Which component carries the information supplied by the observed data?
solution: The likelihood $f(x \mid \theta)$ carries the information in the data. The more data there are, the more the likelihood dominates the prior in the posterior.

title: Improper Priors
prompt: Which prior distribution is improper?
options: Uniform distribution on the real line
solution: A uniform prior over the real line does not integrate to one.

title: MAP Estimation
prompt: Which quantity is maximised in maximum a posteriori estimation?
solution: MAP estimation maximises the posterior.

title: Bayesian Analogue of a Confidence Interval
prompt: Which Bayesian concept corresponds most closely to a frequentist confidence interval?
solution: Credible intervals represent probability statements about parameters.
